scorecard.rationale: The Isfahan trial randomized 92 adults with Parkinson disease and directly compared orally consumed ground dried Sargol stigma powder with placebo. The adjusted DASS depression difference was −4.58 points (95% CI −8.34 to −0.81), favoring less depression. The ground powder was delivered in a fixed-dose tablet. Depression was a secondary endpoint and the trial was powered for a biomarker. An independent Tehran trial favors saffron on Hamilton depression scores, with two other depression measures inconclusive and capsule processing unverified. The Shiraz non-Parkinson stigma adjunct comparison is inconclusive and the isolated crocin mouse result is indirect. The matched Parkinson comparison supports easing and therefore opposes the frozen worsening claim. Effects at ordinary meal quantities and independent replication with the same preparation remain open. Full reports of fibromyalgia stigma extract versus duloxetine and burning-mouth crocin versus citalopram add two independent active-comparator cohorts with inconclusive mood contrasts. Both used nonculinary preparations outside Parkinson disease. The carotenoid review points to a 40-person hydroalcoholic saffron stigma extract versus fluoxetine pilot. Both arms improved, with week-six between-group change p=.10. The active comparison has no placebo arm and does not establish equivalence. It does not change the direction from the ground-stigma Parkinson trial.
